title: dynamic-batching-seqlen-bucketing-padding-heuristics-v15
author: Asha Kapoor
release_notes: Improve dynamic batching heuristics: sequence-length bucketing and padding-minimization. Results: ~18% reduction in padded tokens on mixed workloads, ~12% p99 latency improvement, ~9% throughput uplift. Backwards compatible config with rollout gates.
description: Context: Ongoing effort to reduce wasted compute from padding and to make continuous batching more workload-adaptive. Prior iterations (v12..v14) introduced bucketing and heuristics; this PR refines boundaries, adds runtime histogram smoothing, and tightens KV-cache-aware padding gates. Motivation: reduce per-token cost and p99 latency variability on mixed-length request streams (chat + long-document use cases). Summary of changes: - Bucketing: introduce exponential+linear hybrid bucket generation that adapts to observed seqlen histogram. New algorithm keeps small-seq bins fine-grained and coalesces long-tail lengths. - Padding minimization: only allow padding within a bucket when the expected padding reduction > configurable threshold. Adds per-bucket dynamic padding threshold (configurable via runtime flags). - KV-cache-aware scheduling: short sequences with warm KV caches are grouped preferentially to reduce cold-KV overhead; long sequences get dedicated scheduling to avoid head-of-line blocking. - Kernel selection hinting: when sequences in a batch are all under 64 tokens, scheduler prefers the low-latency int8 kernel path when model quantization is enabled. - Continuous batching: tighter max-wait heuristics with histogram smoothing to avoid oscillation under bursty traffic; cross-batch padding limit prevents pathological padding spikes. - Metrics and observability: new metrics (batch_padding_tokens, bucket_distribution, seqlen_histogram_percentiles) and dashboards. - Safety and rollback: feature gated behind runtime flag dyn_batch.v15 and rollout strategy configured in Redwood Console; default disabled for Dedicated customers until canary passes. Performance: on perf-canary mixed workload (50% chat ~30-80 tokens, 30% short Q/A ~5-30 tokens, 20% long docs >512 tokens) we measured: - padded token reduction: 18% overall (std 3%) - p99 latency: 12% improvement - throughput (tokens/sec): +9% - KV-cache hit consistency improved reducing cold-KV artifacts in p95 by ~7% Testing: - unit tests for bucket generation and padding threshold logic - microbench harness for kernel selection (bench/kernel_select_bench) - integration tests in perf-canary and redwood-quickstarts updated - end-to-end smoke on redwood/private canary - Load test: 24h mixed workload run in perf-canary with canary-config dyn_batch.v15=true Results logged in Linear ENG-1423. Rollout plan: canary in prod for 48h on region-us-west-2 with telemetry gates (padding_tokens, p99 increase <3% rollback), then staged rollout per-customer with opt-in for Dedicated. If any regression, revert via runtime flag and open rollback PR. Related: builds on work from v12..v14; references ENG-1423, ENG-1550, ENG-1689 and SUP-874 (customer report about high padding waste).

review_conversation: Miguel Santos: Nice refinement. Two questions: how does hybrid bucket react to sudden traffic shifts?
Asha Kapoor: We added histogram smoothing (EMA over 30s) and a small stabilization window to avoid oscillation; details in code comments.
Priya Shah: Can we expose per-customer overrides for Dedicated?
Asha Kapoor: Yes, we added runtime flag exposure and Console toggle; default off for Dedicated until opt-in canary.
Evan Liu: microbench looks good. Please add an integration test for KV-cache warm/cold behavior.
Asha Kapoor: Added perf-canary load test and an integration smoke that asserts KV-cache consistency metric.
notes_for_ops: Feature gated via dyn_batch.v15. To enable: set runtime flag and restart batcher service; Console rollout config provided. Watch metrics: batch_padding_tokens, bucket_distribution, seqlen_histogram_percentiles, p99_latency. Canary config in perf-canary repo. If regression: flip dyn_batch.v15=false and re-run canary.
